notesStmt.note: This scrap was almost certainly inscribed sometime in 1888, as that year is indicated both explicitly and in Whitman's reference to being 69 years old (he turned 69 on May 31, 1888).

This manuscript seems to be a draft of titles for the group of poems included in November Boughs (1888) and subsequent printings of Leaves of Grass under the title "Sands at Seventy." Whitman's exact intention for this bit of text isn't clear, since he was gathering and preparing to publish his more recently written poems as "annexes" to several different volumes, almost simultaneously, in 1888: November Boughs, Complete Poems & Prose, and a reprinting of Leaves. It is also possible that the current manuscript was created in the process of preparing advertising copy for one of those books, since such ads also made reference to the newly collected poems as "annexes." At some point, a collector had this manuscript mounted with a Frederick Gutekunst photograph of the poet. Because of this, the verso of the manuscript is partobscured.
